meaning: The census number for the tribe of Naphtali in the second counting
description: The number 45400 is the count of fighting men in the tribe of Naphtali as recorded during the second census on the plains of Moab, just before entering the promised land (Num 26:50). At the first muster in the wilderness of Sinai, Naphtali numbered 53400 men (Num 1:43), which means a decrease of 8000 men during the wilderness journey. This reduction may reflect God's judgment on that generation who refused to enter Canaan. Naphtali was the son of Jacob and Bilhah, Rachel's servant woman, and the tribe received its inheritance in northern Galilee—an area that later gained messianic significance through the prophet Isaiah's words that "the people walking in darkness" will see a great light (Isa 9:1–2). That Naphtali's tribe, despite the decline, remained a significant force at the border of Canaan testifies to God's faithful preservation of His covenant people throughout the wilderness period.

footnotes.text: The name Naphtali means "my struggle" or "I have struggled," from Hebrew נַפְתָּלִי (Naftali), linked to Rachel's words when he was born: "With great struggles I have struggled" (Gen 30:8).

The decline from 53,400 to 45,400 (about 15%) places Naphtali among the tribes that experienced a noticeable reduction between the two censuses. By comparison, Manasseh grew by over 20,000 in the same period.

In Jacob's blessing, Naphtali is described as "a doe set free that bears beautiful fawns" (Gen 49:21), which rabbinic tradition has interpreted as a symbol of fertility and eloquence, and as a prophecy concerning the fertile region of Gennesaret that the tribe received as its inheritance.
Naphtali's territory in Galilee later became the location of much of Jesus' ministry, and Matthew quotes Isaiah 8:23–9:1 as fulfilled by Jesus' work in this area (Matt 4:13–16).
